verification.markdown:
Checked 2026-09-25 by verification agent (sweep #2). Laws cited as of Sep 2026. **Method note:** WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted). Job 1 was done by primary-host fetch, not search, using four sources:
- history lines on law.lis.virginia.gov for every cited section;
- keyword searches of **approved/enacted 2026 Regular Session bill text** on lis.virginia.gov (the official LIS bill search, run in a browser; 1,132 approved bills). The keywords were "chimney" (0 hits), "carbon monoxide" (1 hit: HB507, data-center generator emissions, not residential), "Board for Contractors" (4 hits) and "home solicitation";
- the DPOR Board for Contractors page;
- the DHCD codes page.

- **Licensing threshold, § 54.1-1100:** RE-CONFIRMED. Class C is "over $1,000 but less than $30,000" (or under $250,000 per 12 months). Class B is $30,000 to under $150,000. Class A is $150,000 or more. The history ends "2025, cc. 127, 133", with no 2026 amendment. Source: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title54.1/chapter11/section54.1-1100/. Evidence class GOV.
- **Recovery Fund, § 54.1-1123:** RE-CONFIRMED at $30,000 per claimant per transaction and $100,000 per regulant per biennium. The history ends "2025, cc. 127, 133". **New finding:** 2026 SB565 (Acts 2026 c. 508, approved 4/8/2026, effective 7/1/2026) applies the 2025 limits retroactively to verified claims filed on or after June 6, 2024. Sources: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title54.1/chapter11/section54.1-1123/ ; https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20261/SB565. Evidence class GOV.
- **Seller disclosure, § 55.1-703:** RE-CONFIRMED as a buyer-beware notice with no chimney item. **New finding:** 2026 Acts cc. 308, 309 and 510 amended the section. There is now a version "effective until January 1, 2027" and a version "effective January 1, 2027", which adds item 20 on use-value assessment and roll-back taxes. Neither version mentions chimney, fireplace, flue, wood stove, smoke or CO. Source: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title55.1/chapter7/section55.1-703/. Evidence class GOV.
- **CO law:** RE-CONFIRMED.
  - § 55.1-1229(E): "Upon written request of a tenant in a dwelling unit, the landlord shall install a carbon monoxide alarm in the tenant's dwelling unit within 90 days". The last amendment was 2024 c. 46.
  - § 55.1-1227(A)(9): tenants may not tamper with the alarm.
  - The only 2026 enacted bill-text hit for "carbon monoxide" is HB507 (data centers), which is not residential.
  - The USBC section is still cited generically.
  - Sources: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title55.1/chapter12/section55.1-1229/ ; https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacodefull/title55.1/chapter12/article3/. Evidence class GOV.
- **3-day cancel, § 59.1-21.3:** RE-CONFIRMED. The buyer may cancel "until midnight of the third business day after the day on which the buyer signs an agreement or offer to purchase". The history is 1970, c. 668; 1972, c. 448, with no amendment since. Source: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title59.1/chapter2.1/section59.1-21.3/. Evidence class GOV.
- **Code cycle:** RE-CONFIRMED. DHCD says the 2021 USBC has been effective since Jan 18, 2024, and the DHCD page announces no 2024-cycle date. HBAV (REF, Aug 5, 2026) says the 2024 USBC is "tentatively scheduled to take effect in October 2027", with mandatory compliance expected in October 2028. That REF-only date is kept labeled. Sources: https://www.dhcd.virginia.gov/codes (GOV) ; https://hbav.com/news/update-2024-virginia-building-code-development-cycle (REF).
- **2026 law-change sweep:** done by primary-host fetch, not search. Findings:
  - SB565 / c. 508 (Recovery Fund retroactivity, above).
  - HB165 (2026, enacted): Board for Contractors exams available in alternative languages.
  - HB1439 / SB823 (2026, enacted): regulation of solar installation companies. Not chimney-related.
  - § 55.1-703 2026 amendments (above).
  - DPOR's contractors page notes a $7.25/yr technology fee under 2026 HB30, effective July 1, 2026 (administrative).
  - No 2026 change to §§ 54.1-1100, 54.1-1123, 55.1-1229 or 59.1-21.3.
  - No enacted 2026 bill text contains "chimney".
  - Sources: https://lis.virginia.gov/session-details/20261/statistics/status ; https://www.dpor.virginia.gov/Boards/Contractors. Evidence class GOV.
- **Mirror spot-check:** n/a (Virginia is not a mirror state; all cites are on law.lis.virginia.gov).
- **Dead links:** none. All of these resolved on Sep 25: law.lis §§ 54.1-1100, 54.1-1123, 55.1-703, 55.1-1229, 59.1-21.3, vacodefull 55.1 ch. 12 art. 3, dhcd.virginia.gov/codes, hbav.com and legiscan HB1707. The legiscan page is REF; the official equivalent is Acts 2025 c. 127.

sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence; tiered exam license)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.markdown: Virginia runs a **statewide, tiered contractor license with real exams** through **DPOR's Board for Contractors** (Va. Code Title 54.1, Chapter 11). **A license is required for contracting work valued over $1,000** (§ 54.1-1100: Class C starts at "over $1,000"). Three classes by value, as amended by **2025 HB1707**: **Class C** (single contract over $1,000 but under $30,000, or under $250,000 in 12 months), **Class B** ($30,000 to under $150,000 per contract, or $250,000 to under $1 million in 12 months), **Class A** ($150,000+ per contract or $1 million+ in 12 months) (law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title54.1/chapter11/section54.1-1100/). *(Per-class experience years and exam waivers not re-read on a primary page in Sep 2026 — verify before publishing specifics.)* Two exam tracks: the **designated employee** passes the Virginia Contractor Law/business portion; the **qualified individual** passes a **trade exam per classification/specialty** (Building, HVAC, etc.). Home improvement / masonry chimney work runs under a Building or Home Improvement specialty. Financial-responsibility requirements plus a Recovery Fund contribution apply *(specific net-worth/bond figures UNVERIFIED — do not publish numbers)*. Public lookup: **dpor.virginia.gov** license search.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: The trade exam is **by classification (Building code, HVAC code, etc.) — not chimney/flue diagnosis or sweep competence.** A Class A Building contractor may never have scanned a flue. Individual certs (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) remain the competence signal on top of the license.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV — high confidence; the quirk)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.markdown: Virginia's disclosure is the strangest of the launch set: a **mandatory form that discloses nothing about condition.** Under the **Virginia Residential Property Disclosure Act (Va. Code § 55.1-700 et seq.; § 55.1-703)**, the seller must deliver a **Residential Property Disclosure Statement — but it is a "buyer beware" notice**: the owner "makes no representations or warranties as to the condition," and the buyer is advised to "exercise whatever due diligence [the] purchaser deems necessary, including obtaining a home inspection." **There is no chimney line item because the form lists no property conditions at all.** (The statement's content is set by § 55.1-703(B) and posted by the Real Estate Board on its website; 2026 Acts cc. 308, 309 and 510 amended the section — the version effective Jan 1, 2027 adds a twentieth "no representations" item on use-value assessment/roll-back taxes — and neither the current nor the 2027 version mentions a chimney, fireplace, flue, wood stove, smoke or CO item.) Virginia is caveat emptor with a mandatory notice that says so in writing. No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown: Two-track, like Maryland. **(1) The Contractor Transaction Recovery Fund (Va. Code § 54.1-1118 et seq.)** pays a homeowner with an unpaid judgment against a *licensed* contractor **up to $30,000 per claimant per single transaction** (§ 54.1-1123; raised from $20,000 by 2025 HB1707 / Acts 2025 cc. 127 and 133, approved Mar 19, 2025) with an **aggregate cap of $100,000 per regulant per biennium** (raised from $40,000 by the same acts); actual loss only. **2026 SB565 (Acts 2026 c. 508, effective July 1, 2026)** extends those higher limits to any claimant who filed a verified claim on or after June 6, 2024 that the Board later approved — the dollar caps themselves did not change. **(2) The Virginia Consumer Protection Act (§ 59.1-196 et seq.; § 59.1-204)** gives actual damages or $500 (whichever greater), and for **willful** violations up to **treble damages** (or $1,000) plus attorney's fees — discretionary, moderate. Home-solicitation/door-to-door sales carry a **3-business-day right to cancel** (Home Solicitation Sales Act, Va. Code § 59.1-21.1 et seq.; cancellation right at **§ 59.1-21.3**, until midnight of the third business day after signing). Complaints: DPOR + AG.

sections.rawHeading: 5 · Permits & codes (GOV — high on uniformity; confirm cycle)
sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.markdown: Virginia has a **statewide Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC, Va. Code § 36-97 et seq.)**, IRC-based and **genuinely uniform** — VA is a Dillon-rule state, so localities enforce but cannot materially amend the code (a real contrast to home-rule patchworks like Ohio). The **2021 USBC (2021 I-Code base) has been in effect since Jan 18, 2024** (dhcd.virginia.gov/codes); the 2024 USBC is tentatively slated for **October 2027** with a one-year transition (REF: HBAV, Aug 5, 2026 — confirm with DHCD when adopted). Chimney relines, rebuilds, crowns, and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally **permit work** through the local building official; routine sweeps and like-for-like caps generally are not.

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO law (GOV — medium; code + rental, no pre-sale certificate)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.confidenceNote: medium; code + rental, no pre-sale certificate
sections.markdown: The USBC requires CO detection in new construction with fuel-fired appliances/attached garage, *(exact VRC section number not read in Sep 2026 — cite "USBC" generically)*, and the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act requires that **"Upon written request of a tenant in a dwelling unit, the landlord shall install a carbon monoxide alarm in the tenant's dwelling unit within 90 days"** (landlord may recover reasonable costs) — **Va. Code § 55.1-1229(E)**; tenants may not tamper with a landlord-installed CO alarm (§ 55.1-1227(A)(9)). **No statewide mandatory pre-sale CO certificate.** A permitted chimney job remains the natural moment to add alarms.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: No statewide burn-ban or stove-emission regime. Not a material content section for VA.

sections.rawHeading: 8 · Scam landscape (REF — partial; pull specifics before publish)
sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: DPOR disciplines licensees and the AG enforces the VCPA; the door-knock "we noticed your chimney" pitch is a textbook Home Solicitation Sales Act / VCPA scenario, and unlicensed contracting over $1,000 is itself an offense. **Specific VA chimney-sweep enforcement actions: NOT YET CONFIRMED — re-run search before publish.**

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Mixed climate — colder in the western mountains, milder in Tidewater/Hampton Roads. Burn season ~Oct–Mar (longer in the west). Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

sections.title: Price seeding (internal)
sections.markdown: Northern Virginia (Fairfax, Loudoun, Arlington — DC metro) runs **well above national**; the rest of the state nearer or below national. Regionalize sharply for NoVA.

sections.title: /rights table row (internal)
sections.markdown: License: **YES — DPOR tiered license (Class A/B/C), required for work over $1,000; Class C <$30k, B $30k–<$150k, A $150k+ (post-HB1707)** · Registration: **license regime + Contractor Transaction Recovery Fund (up to $30k)** · Disclosure law: **mandatory form but BUYER-BEWARE — no condition content (§ 55.1-703)** · Chimney item on form: **none (form discloses nothing)** · 3-day cancel: **YES (Home Solicitation Sales Act § 59.1-21.1)** · CO law: **code (USBC) + rental-on-request within 90 days (§ 55.1-1229(E)); no pre-sale certificate** · Lookup: dpor.virginia.gov

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: Virginia is the **"strong license, non-disclosing disclosure"** state. DPOR runs a genuine tiered exam license (a Class A contractor cleared a trade exam and a law exam) backed by a **$30,000 recovery fund** — peer to Maryland's regime. Yet Virginia's mandatory seller "disclosure" is a **buyer-beware notice that reveals nothing about the chimney and tells you, in writing, to inspect it yourself.** So Virginia and Massachusetts reach the same buyer from opposite directions: MA has no disclosure form; VA has a form whose entire content is "there is no disclosure." Against the ladder — VA licenses (like MD/MI), Ohio doesn't; and VA's protection, like Maryland's, lives in the *contractor* license and recovery fund, not the sale. The competence gap holds: the trade exam is by code classification, never chimney-specific.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Virginia?
faq.a: State licensing: YES — DPOR tiered license (Class A/B/C), required for work over $1,000; Class C <$30k, B $30k–<$150k, A $150k+ (post-HB1707). Registration or credential: license regime + Contractor Transaction Recovery Fund (up to $30k). Seller disclosure at sale: mandatory form but BUYER-BEWARE — no condition content (§ 55.1-703). Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES (Home Solicitation Sales Act § 59.1-21.1). Carbon monoxide alarm law: code (USBC) + rental-on-request within 90 days (§ 55.1-1229(E)); no pre-sale certificate. Where to check a contractor: dpor.virginia.gov. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.
